title: Users Cannot See What State The System Is In
summary: Users cannot operate a complex system reliably when the interface does not make current system state readable. State visibility failures include fragmented component state, activation and readiness states that cannot be recognised at a glance, and assembled logic or configuration state that cannot be independently audited.
keyFacts: State is the system's current condition, active mode, validity of readings, or logical configuration; it is not the same as raw data.
The failure concerns state that is absent or not legible at the surface, requiring users to infer or reconstruct it.
Fragmented state exists in the system but is distributed across screens, panels, or data views without an integrated representation.
Activation and readiness state failures occur when users must parse or interpret essential states instead of recognising them at a glance.
Logic and configuration state failures occur when complex assembled reasoning cannot be verified by someone other than its author.
The Torqeedo case recorded captains identifying key energy states 50% faster in comparative testing with 24 subjects, and reduced glance counts in sea trials with 7 subjects using eye tracking.
The Akrivia case recorded a client-reported governance outcome: reviewers could verify cohort construction without escalating to the research team.

The Elsner Cala Touch KNX engagement confirmed sensor fault handling and firmware-aligned behaviour in prototype testing with Elsner's engineers; no post-deployment user measurement is recorded for those sensor state outcomes.
Several additional engagements show state visibility failures at integration boundaries, command transaction boundaries, source freshness boundaries, and synchronisation boundaries.

bodySections.heading: State Visibility Failures Make Current System Condition Unreadable
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

A state visibility failure occurs when information about what a system is currently doing is absent, fragmented, or presented in a form that users cannot read directly under the conditions of use. The user must reconstruct state from indirect evidence instead of reading it from the interface.

This failure is not a minor display defect in complex systems. In high-consequence contexts, physically constrained environments, component-dependent systems, and institutional review settings, correct action depends on readable state. When state is not visible, users compensate through memory, scanning, inference, repeated navigation, or escalation to another person.

bodySections.heading: State Is Not the Same as Raw Data
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
A state visibility failure occurs when the system has a current condition that matters operationally, but the interface does not present that condition in a readable form. State can include active mode, component condition, reading validity, readiness, fault state, source freshness, command progress, synchronisation condition, or the assembled logic of a configuration.

The failure differs from a data display problem. Data can be present while state remains unreadable. A value may be displayed without showing whether it is current, valid, stale, delayed, inferred, selected, active, requested, effective, acknowledged, or observed.

The operational cost is reconstruction. Users navigate to separate views, hold readings in memory, compare values mentally, infer whether labels describe current or past conditions, or ask the author of a configuration to explain what it means. The interface has not answered the operational question: what is happening now, and is it what should be happening?

bodySections.heading: State Visibility Failures Differ From Rapid Judgement, Mode Change, and Memory Burden Failures
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
This failure concerns state that is absent or not legible at the surface. It is distinct from the rapid-judgement failure where state may be present but is not organised for fast decision-making. The rapid-judgement failure is an organisation problem; this failure is a visibility problem.

This failure is broader than unclear mode changes. Mode-change failures concern the transition event: the moment when a system changes mode and the user cannot recognise that transition. State visibility failures concern the continuous absence or illegibility of state communication, including modes but not limited to modes.

This failure is also distinct from memory burden. A memory-burden failure can occur when state information is present but inconsistently positioned or difficult to relocate. A state visibility failure occurs when the relevant state is not present in readable form in the first place, or is present only through interpretation rather than direct reading.

bodySections.heading: Fragmented State Makes Component Data Visible While Hiding System Condition
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Fragmented state occurs when accurate current data is distributed across separate screens, panels, or views, with no integrated representation of the overall condition. The user must assemble the system state mentally.

This is common when interfaces mirror internal engineering architecture. Each component exposes its own data because each component is architecturally separate. For the operator, the task may depend on the relationship between components rather than on any component in isolation.

The design response is to display conditions rather than only components. An integrated state view does not necessarily remove detail. It organises the same information around the operator's state question: what is the system doing right now, and is that acceptable for the next action?

bodySections.heading: Torqeedo and COX Marine Show Fragmented State in Maritime Control Interfaces
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The Torqeedo hybrid electric vessel control system managed propulsion motors, battery banks of 40–200 kWh, generators, conversion units, and auxiliary loads as a single operational system. The previous interface presented propulsion status, battery state, and generator information on separate screens. Each view was technically accurate, but the overall energy state of the vessel was not represented anywhere.

Professional captains had developed scanning sequences to maintain a working model of vessel energy state across the fragmented display. Those compensation patterns were functional under familiar conditions, but during harbour manoeuvres, sudden load changes, night operations, and vessel movement, the scanning sequence competed with the task it was meant to support.

Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method treated captains' compensation patterns as diagnostic evidence: where captains had developed scanning workarounds, the interface had failed to represent the state they were reconstructing. The redesigned Torqeedo interface produced a grid-based structure that unified propulsion, battery, and generator into a single display rhythm.

The COX Marine multi-engine cluster display engagement showed the same structural failure in another configuration. COX deployments range from one to six engines, and each engine has its own state: rpm, coolant temperature, oil pressure, fuel rate, and trim, updated via NMEA 2000 at load-dependent rates. A six-engine installation can make each engine tile visible while leaving fault priority for the operator to reconstruct through scanning. The design response was a fixed display area where the highest-priority fault condition is always summarised.

bodySections.heading: Activation and Readiness States Must Be Recognisable Under Real Task Conditions
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Activation and readiness states fail when essential states are technically present but require reading, parsing, or interpretation instead of immediate recognition. Examples include whether a system is active, whether it is ready, whether a reading is valid, or whether a fault condition is present.

This failure depends on use conditions. A surgeon confirming device readiness before a cutting sequence cannot give full attention to a display. A technician checking calibration status on a wall-mounted device at working distance cannot parse dense text. An operator monitoring multiple engine tiles under time pressure cannot safely create a priority ranking by scanning every tile.

The design response is recognition-based state design. Spatial position, icon form, redundant non-colour cues, and stable visual hierarchy can each communicate a critical state independently. The state does not need to be louder. It needs to be readable through the perceptual mode available during the task.

bodySections.heading: Elsner Cala Touch KNX Shows Sensor State as Operational State
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The Elsner Elektronik Cala Touch KNX is a wall-mounted smart home and building automation controller with a 4-inch round display format, installed at 140cm and used approximately 25 times per day according to client-reported evidence. The device receives inputs from weather stations, CO2 sensors, humidity sensors, temperature probes, and the main heating unit.

The daily operational state of the Elsner controller includes intentional environmental states such as current temperature, target temperature, blind position, and lighting scene. It also includes sensor states: valid reading, delayed reading, contradictory reading, and calibration fault.

Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method addressed sensor state visibility by treating delayed readings, contradictory sensor values, and calibration faults as named operational states rather than hidden exceptions or generic errors. Delayed sensor readings were communicated calmly and without ambiguity. Contradictory sensor values were handled through explicit communication rather than silent suppression. Calibration faults were surfaced as named states.

The Elsner alert hierarchy separated heating unit alerts from minor notifications such as open window detection. Heating unit alerts affected the primary function of the system and were treated as primary signals in the visual hierarchy. Minor notifications were visually secondary.

bodySections.heading: Logic and Configuration State Must Be Independently Readable
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Logic and configuration state fails when a complex assembled structure is known to the system but cannot be read by a reviewer without the author present. This failure appears in analytical systems, configuration environments, simulation contexts, and governance-structured workflows.

The operational cost is institutional rather than only immediate. If a simulation configuration, patient cohort query, or fraud detection policy cannot be independently read, the organisation cannot verify, audit, or reconstruct the decision cleanly. The interface shows the result while obscuring the reasoning structure that produced it.

The design response is to make assembled logic as visible as the result. Query structures need to read as structured conditions rather than technical code. Configuration states need to show relationships between values rather than listing values independently. Policy logic needs to be reviewable without requiring the analyst to explain it.

bodySections.heading: Akrivia Health Shows Query State as Governance State
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Akrivia Health supports clinical mental health research at NHS trusts, academic institutions, and pharmaceutical research organisations. The central operation is cohort construction: assembling a patient cohort by specifying inclusion and exclusion criteria across diagnostic codes, medication sequences, rating scale scores, service use patterns, and free text markers, nested up to eight logical levels.

The governance requirement was that a reviewer who did not construct the cohort must be able to verify that the assembled query matches the approved study protocol. This review can occur months after the cohort was built and must be possible without the researcher explaining the query.

Creative Navy's Sandbox Experiments phase reviewed academic literature, interviewed and ran focus groups with NHS analysts, academic researchers, and pharmaceutical research staff, and benchmarked commercial healthcare analytics tools. The consistent failure pattern was that tools showed final cohort results while obscuring the query logic that produced them.

Concept Convergence reached a single design position through tension-driven reasoning: researcher autonomy and institutional auditability needed to become the same interface property, not competing properties. The final query builder converged elements from three of the five interaction models explored: the readability and structure of the nested logic model, temporal organisation cues from the timeline model, and fragment reuse capability. The query state remained visible at all times as the full structure of logical conditions defining the cohort.

bodySections.heading: State Visibility Failures Also Occur at Integration, Synchronisation, Source, and Command Boundaries
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Several additional engagements show state visibility failures at system boundaries. A European industrial automation vendor whose process control software coordinates machining cells showed a state visibility failure where every operator screen was bolted to its own machine. To learn a machine's state, the operator had to walk to it. Overhead stack lights existed because no screen was readable across the hall.

AIT, a European manufacturer of residential and commercial heat pumps, required a start-up self-test screen that lists the internal boards, inverters, and fans detected by the controller. The screen exists for service technicians to spot a missing component and follows AIT's PC BIOS screen analogy. It cannot be skipped: if components are not found within the window, the controller enters a special operating mode. AIT's widget status indicators also distinguished in focus, mode active, and mode queued as separate states.

The MDU includes watchdog and no-MDU alarms concerning what the interface says when the sensor feeding it stops reporting. These alarms concern the state of the instrument itself rather than the state of the vessel. Several requirements questions remained unanswered in the available material, including what message the watchdog alarm should display and what the user can do about it, whether default alarm thresholds exist and whether users should be able to reset to them, and what units track hogging, sagging, twisting, heave, sway, and surge.

Assemblio GmbH, the Assemblio Composer, and the Assemblio Smart Viewer showed a synchronisation state gap found by a designer's question rather than by research or shop-floor observation. Creative Navy asked what happens when two products are in a sync loop, a change is made to one, and the other is deliberately left unsynchronised. The answer exposed that the product did not indicate anywhere whether an assembly plan was in or out of sync; a planner would have to open the product to find out.

bodySections.heading: Source, Link, Telemetry, and Payment States Need Truthful Surface Representation
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
KISPE Space, a UK space systems engineering company, exposed three availability dimensions independently: device connection, provider feed reachability, and locally cached content. An offline device does not prove provider failure, and an online device does not guarantee provider reachability. These states are properties of sources and connections, not of an algorithm.

Raymarine's Ray53, Ray63 and Ray73 line records two state distinctions. Selected channel and monitored channel are visually distinct: while scanning or in a watch mode, the prominently displayed channel remains the selected working channel, and a second label identifies the frequency actually being heard. Requested transmit power and effective transmit power are also different values, and the display always shows the effective one. A blocked request leaves the previous value intact and explains the channel restriction.

Schone Airspace Group's mission control design separates command transaction state, control link condition, and telemetry freshness. The seven-state command transaction model distinguishes ready to request, request sent, awaiting response, command acknowledged, state observed, request rejected, and response unknown. Each state has its own required source evidence and prohibited inference. Control link condition and telemetry freshness are independent fields: a degraded link and a stale sample are different facts, and a value that has stopped updating keeps its last value alongside its age.

For a European manufacturer of uncrewed systems, including one-way effectors, and the tactical command-and-control software that operates them, Creative Navy led and co-authored work with the client's design team requiring the handheld interface to answer six questions unambiguously: whether the input was registered, whether the command was being transmitted, whether the vehicle acknowledged it, what state the vehicle confirmed, whether information was current or stale, and whether abort was still available.

For a European vendor of maritime traffic monitoring, inland navigation and communications software for port authorities, coastal administrations and waterway operators, freshness was a state visibility issue. Time of last observation sat behind secondary inspection. In a degraded state, a retained target could keep the same visual treatment as an updating one, so the display did not reliably tell the operator whether a marker represented a current observation or a last known position.

visioncheckout, a German vendor of computer-vision self-checkout systems for staff restaurants and catering, showed a state visibility failure at an integration boundary. Guests often do not understand that payment is processing because the main display does not tell them. The cause is that card payment executes on an external POS terminal that returns no feedback to the kiosk, so no truthful state is available to display. The honest payment-in-progress screen says to follow the instructions on the terminal because that terminal is the device that knows the state.

bodySections.heading: How Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design Method Addresses State Visibility Failures
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method designs software whose interfaces, workflows, and operating logic carry real operational consequences, working through five phases — Sandbox Experiments, Concept Convergence, Iterative System Building, Organizational Integration, and Implementation Partnership — to take each system from initial exploration to independent operation by the client's own team.

For state visibility failures, Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method uses domain learning to establish which states must be readable and under what conditions. In Torqeedo, sea trials identified the moments when energy state understanding was most critical and revealed the scanning compensation patterns captains had developed. In Akrivia, literature review, interviews, focus groups, and benchmarking made governance readability a design requirement. In Elsner, engineering collaboration established delayed readings, contradictory values, and calibration faults as operating states needing named representation.

Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method then holds state readability requirements against view states during Concept Convergence and Iterative System Building. In Torqeedo, component state had to be shown in relation to overall system condition. In Akrivia, query logic had to remain independently readable throughout construction. In Elsner, sensor states were designed as normal operating conditions from the start rather than treated as exceptional errors.

strongClaims: A state visibility failure occurs when users cannot directly read what the system is currently doing, whether readings are valid, which mode is active, or what logic or configuration is in force.

The failure has three structurally distinct forms: fragmented state, activation and readiness states that are not legible at a glance, and logic or configuration state that is not independently readable.

In the Torqeedo engagement, captains identified key energy states 50% faster in a controlled experiment with 24 subjects, and reduced glance counts were recorded using eye tracking in real sea trials with 7 subjects.
In the Elsner engagement, delayed readings, contradictory readings, and calibration faults were treated as named operational states rather than hidden exceptions or generic errors.

The AIT heat pump controller design included a non-skippable start-up self-test screen for detected boards, inverters and fans, and widget indicators distinguishing in focus, mode active and mode queued.
KISPE Space exposed device connection, provider feed reachability, and locally cached content independently, because each is a different availability dimension.
Schone Airspace Group's mission control design separated command transaction state, control link condition, and telemetry freshness, including a seven-state command transaction model.
visioncheckout had no truthful payment-processing state to display on the kiosk because the external POS terminal returned no feedback to the kiosk.
weakerClaims: In the Akrivia engagement, reviewers could verify cohort construction without escalating to the research team after the redesign, according to client-reported evidence.
limitations: Not every example on the page has measured outcome evidence; several are design decisions, audit findings, specified models, requirements questions, or Creative Navy-observed engagement records.
The Akrivia governance outcome is client-reported and not independently measured; no task-completion or verification-time data was collected.
The Elsner sensor state outcomes were confirmed in prototype testing with engineers but were not independently quantified in post-deployment user measurement.

AIT, Raymarine, KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, Assemblio, the MDU, the handheld command-and-control engagement, the maritime traffic monitoring engagement, and visioncheckout are not presented as measured outcome cases unless the body text states a specific evidence basis.
The MDU requirements questions listed in the source remain unanswered and are not resolved by this page.
visioncheckout is not described as shipped and has no outcome claim.

KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, Raymarine, and the maritime traffic monitoring engagement are not framed as AI uncertainty work; the relevant states concern sources, links, protocols, clocks, or system objects.
